name: Hourly Aspen run checks and recovery
prompt:
Check the remaining RL/MPC experiment runs in this chat every hour and make necessary, narrowly scoped repairs within the user's authorization. Work in C:\Users\hamediaa\OneDrive - McMaster University\PythonProjects\RL_assisted_MPC. Start with RUN_RECOVERY_STATUS.md and the current recovery manifests so that superseded failed attempts are not mistaken for current jobs. Include the column repetitions, all five column E1 configurations, the combined coordinator, the horizon recovery supervisor, and automatic Aspen retention. Determine completed, progressing, pending and failed runs using actual process creation identities, CPU/progress changes, append-only logs, current checkpoint metadata and saved result files. Native comparison applications can legitimately pause, and expected process recycling or Windows RPC diagnostics alone do not prove that a scientific run failed.

Use lightweight checks. For replaceable live JSON/checkpoint metadata use the existing snapshot-alias readers in aspen_retention.py after checking that the file is stable; do not hold read handles on the original replaceable files or unnecessarily read live shared queue manifests. Check memory commitment headroom and free disk space. Retention state and verified archives are at C:\Users\hamediaa\RL_MPC_local_archive\aspen_retention_20261023. Horizon recovery is at Distillation\Results\state_recovery\20261023_horizon_native_process, with acceptance evidence in change-reports\horizon_recovery_20261023. Preserve the latest two verified complete matched Python/native checkpoints, pinned recovery dependencies, every scientific result and all retained lossless archives.

If a run actually fails, diagnose the underlying error, verify and back up its full recovery state, and recover only that failed run on an available reserved Aspen case using the existing private numerical runtime and fresh-owned-process recovery wrappers. Verify learner/controller and native restoration, use a bounded continuation when needed, and require at least 6 GiB commitment headroom before launching. Do not restart training from scratch, duplicate a live or memory-gated launch, interrupt healthy workers except for the explicitly approved combined-only checkpoint restart when its current Aspen memory warrants it, close an idle application owned by an active run, alter sealed scientific sources or shared queue plans, change global packages, reopen OneDrive syncing, or require administrator access. Preserve the automatic combined queue and retention. Make scoped fixes concrete and tested; if safe recovery is blocked, preserve the data and explain the exact action or decision needed.

The user has explicitly approved a brief checkpoint restart of combined E1 only to release growing Aspen memory. Do not restart combined while its memory is normal. Before a preventive combined restart, refresh and verify the newest two complete matched Python/native checkpoints, back up every result and pinned recovery dependency, confirm current owned process creation identities and preserve all other healthy workers. Use the existing guarded restoration and bounded continuation checks and require at least 6 GiB commitment headroom before relaunch. Never execute the stale earlier preventive plan unchanged.

Keep the existing progress viewer and concise recovery records current. Report meaningful progress, completion, failures, repairs, or a required user decision; remain quiet when the state is unchanged and no action is needed. Once all remaining authorized runs finish and their saved results verify, report completion and disable this hourly check.
